content:
sree: Heads-up — I hit a surprising perf regression when we enable torch.compile + CUDA graphs for our Llama-ish serving path. Baseline (no compile/graphs) at seq=1024 was ~850 tok/s (p50 18ms). With torch.compile + cudagraphs it's ~380 tok/s (p50 42ms).

lee_perf: :thinking: rough. Any profiler traces or kernel lists?

sree: Yep. Quick profiler dump shows attention matmul chosen kernels changed between runs. Looks like the graph-compiled path freezes shapes and that leads the kernel selector to pick a different GEMM/attention kernel. Snippet: 

```
Profiler summary (sample):
aten::matmul        45%   -> gemm_fp16_sm80
flash_attn          30%   -> fused_flash_attn_sm80
aten::matmul        10%   -> matmul_unfused
```

When the cudagraph/compiled graph is used, the fused_flash_attn path drops and we get more generic gemm calls. The kernel chooser seems to treat graph shapes differently and sometimes disables the fused attention kernel (maybe due to stride/contig requirements or different memory layout after compile).

maria_ml: I vaguely remember Inductor emitting different memory formats for some ops under compile which breaks the flash_attn matcher. Did you try forcing the flash_attn kernel?

sree: I tried forcing via env override and the perf comes back. So it's a kernel-selection mismatch triggered by graph/compile. Repro steps below: 

```
# minimal repro
model = torch.compile(model, backend='inductor')
# warm up warmup
for _ in range(10): model(inp, cache)
# capture graph
cg = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
with torch.cuda.graph(cg):
    out = model(inp, cache)
```

Run compare: compiled+graph vs compiled_only vs baseline.

lee_perf: Two hypotheses: (1) torch.compile alters op order / memory layout so the flash-attn matcher doesn't see the pattern; (2) cudagraphs pin shapes which prevents runtime autotuner from trying alternative kernels. Could be both.

tom_runtime: I can reproduce locally on an A100. If cudagraph prevents runtime kernel fallback, we need either: (A) compile separate graphs per sequence-length bucket (so selector can pick correct kernel before graph capture), or (B) re-run a short autotune / kernel probe before capturing the graph and cache that selection keyed on shape signature.

maria_ml: (A) seems heavier but predictable. (B) sounds nice — do we have cheap autotune that finishes in <50ms per new shape? Not usually.

lee_perf: Another option: keep the graph but insert a small dynamic wrapper that calls a specialized fused attention kernel via an explicit path (i.e., bypass matcher). That avoids depending on compile internals. We already have that for some CPU kernels.

infra-bot: perf-run #2026 finished. artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/2026/ (profile + flamegraphs).

sree: Added the artifacts link to the bug. Quick numbers from microbench: 

- baseline (no compile, no graph), seq=1024: 850 tok/s, p50=18ms
- torch.compile only, seq=1024: 830 tok/s, p50=19ms
- torch.compile + cudagraph (single graph), seq=1024: 380 tok/s, p50=42ms
- compile+graph w/ forced flash_attn: 820 tok/s, p50=20ms

tom_runtime: FYI memory layout diff I saw in a trace: compile path inserted a contiguous() for a tensor that flash-attn expects in channels-last-ish layout -> matcher misses.

maria_ml: So practical fixes: 1) make kernel matcher more permissive to contig variants; 2) make runtime record shape->kernel picks pre-graph and persist in our kernel cache; 3) forbid cudagraph capture for shapes we haven't seen before (warm-up policy).

lee_perf: I'm +1 for a hybrid: warm-up to populate kernel-cache (cheap run) then capture graph. Also add logging so we detect when graph capture led to worse kernel picks (compare token/sec after capture), and auto-revert capture.

tom_runtime: I'll prototype a warm-up flow: for each incoming sequence-length bucket, run 3 short inferences with compile but no graph, call our kernel_selector.autotune(shape), persist key (device,sm,seq_len,bs). If success, capture graphs for that bucket. Will measure overhead.

sree: Nice. Action items:
- tom_runtime to open perf issue with repro + profile + patch plan (tom to own)
- lee_perf to write unit test for kernel matcher permissiveness and contig variants
- maria_ml to enumerate common seq_len buckets from production traces (~128/256/512/1024/2048) and share distributions

tom_runtime: will open issue #4326 and ping the infra-bench job once prototype ready. ETA EOW.

maria_ml: if anyone's blocked on this, disabling cudagraphs for seq >= 512 is a safe short-term toggle (we can gate by customer tier).

lee_perf: good. Also capture a small flamegraph of kernel dispatch in the graph vs non-graph path, that helped me pinpoint the matcher failure earlier.

sree: thanks all. attaching the short profile in the issue. Ping me if you need quick repro harness.

tom_runtime: will post microbench results in this thread when I have them. :+1:
